question: Should the focused tests and linked prior failure waive the normal real-behavior proof gate for this session-owner correction, or should this PR provide a redacted after-fix configured-default-agent run before merge?
rationale: The patch is small and follows the stated architecture, but only a real configured-default scenario can show that ClickClack creates and persists the intended owner outside the mocked test path.

options.title: Require runtime proof
options.body: Request a redacted terminal or ClickClack run showing an unqualified key resolving to a configured non-main default and an agent-qualified key retaining its encoded owner.

options.title: Accept test-only evidence
options.body: Treat the focused suite and related release failure as sufficient and merge with the remaining runtime-path uncertainty explicitly accepted.
